controls: This wizard will help you create a self-extracting / self-installing package.

First, you need to create a Self Extraction Directive (SED) file to store information about your package.  If you have already done this, select Open existing one; otherwise, select Create New Self Extraction Directive file.
Create new Self Extraction Directive file.
Open existing Self Extraction Directive file:
2000.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: You have selected an existing Self Extraction Directive file. If you want to make modifications to it, select Modify Self Extraction Directive file; otherwise, you can skip to the package creation page by selecting Create Package.
2001.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: Type the title of your package in the following  box.  This title will appear on all dialog boxes that the user sees.
2002.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: If you want to confirm that the user wants to install your package, select Prompt User With and type the prompt. Otherwise, select No Prompt.
2003.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: If you want to display a License Agreement before allowing an installation, select Display a License and choose the License file; otherwise, select Do Not Display a License.
2004.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: Create a list of files that you want in your compressed package.
2005.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: Select the programs or INF files to launch from the package.  A custom command can also be created below.
The below comand will be run after the install has completed.
2006.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: Select how your installation program's window will be displayed.
2007.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: If you want to display a message to the user after installation is complete, select Display Message and type the message; otherwise, select No Message.
2008.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: Enter the target path and filename for your package.  This is the file that will get downloaded and executed by the user.
Hide File Extracting Progress Animation from User
Store files using Long File Name inside Package
2009.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: If you would like to save this information for later use, select Save Self Extraction Directive (SED) file; otherwise, select Don't save.
If you choose to save this information, you can modify it later and recreate your package, without re-entering all the previous information.
2010.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: You are now ready to create your package.  Click Next to start the process.  It can take several minutes to finish.
Your package has been created.  Click Finish when you are ready to quit.
2011.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: Select final result of the package.
Extract files and run an installation command
2012.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: Select how you want the system to restart at the end of your installation program.
Do not prompt user before restarting
2013.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: Enter a 8.3 format filename for the cabinet (CAB) file. If you choose to build a fixed size CAB file(s), only the first FIVE characters will be used as the file's base name.
Reserve space in the CAB file for Code Signing:
Store files using Long File Name inside Package
2014.title: IExpress Wizard

controls: Enter the layout INF filename.  This generated file depicts the relations between the source files and the Cabinet file.
Enter the label name for the source media.  If installer could not find the file, this is the media name used to prompt user.
2015.title: IExpress Wizard
